beats.text: Genocide by policy — five cinema acts under Rome Statute Article 6. Intent, killing, harm, conditions, coercion. Primary sources only. Canada public record.

This registry establishes a five-part case for investigation under Article 6 of the Rome Statute. The framework relies strictly on the public record: Hansard transcripts, federal statutes, provincial coroner files, and Health Canada data.
This is an active investigation file. Primary sources are cited for every claim. Start at ACT I or review any element.
Intent → Killing → Harm → Conditions → Coercion. Each act presents documentary evidence, demographic data, and primary-source citations.

Bill C-7 knowingly removed the reasonably foreseeable natural death safeguard, expanding state-administered death to the disabled and vulnerable. Parliament was warned of this outcome. The explicit intent to broaden the cohort sits on the Hansard record under Article 6(a).
Primary Source: Statutes of Canada 2021 (Bill C-7) • Track 2 Volume: 776 Canadians in 2024.

Track 2 deaths documented by Ontario’s Chief Coroner confirm the non-terminal cohort. Vulnerable Canadians are being processed through the system while facing compounding pressures of poverty, housing deprivation, and clinical isolation.
Evidence: Ontario MDRC Reports • Scope: ~4.7% of total 2024 MAID volume.

State agencies repeatedly offered MAID to citizens seeking treatment. Veterans Affairs agents proactively suggested death over care, while patients were offered MAID while being denied necessary home support.
Article 6(b): Causing serious harm • Palliative Access: <30% receive needed care.

Track 2 applicants face severe material deprivation before death. They fall into the lowest material-resources (28.4%) and highest residential-instability (48.3%) quintiles, demonstrating death where care and housing should be provided.
Demographics: 61% female (Ontario Track 2) • Article 6(c): Inflicting destructive conditions.

With over 76,000 total MAID provisions, the system has become a default relief valve for a collapsing social safety net. When the only door the state opens without friction ends your life — that is structural coercion.
Impact: 5.1% of all Canadian deaths in 2024 • Result: Policy-driven extermination.
